t:
Part D of title V of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 290dd et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following:“SEC. 549. MENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTREACH AND EDUCATION ON COLLEGE CAMPUSES.“(a) Purpose.—It is the purpose of this section to increase access to, and reduce the stigma associated with, mental health services to ensure that students at institutions of higher education have the support necessary to successfully complete their studies.“(b) National Public Education Campaign.—The Secretary, acting through the Assistant Secretary and in collaboration with the Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, shall convene an interagency, public-private sector working group to plan, establish, and begin coordinating and evaluating a targeted public education campaign that is designed to focus on mental and behavioral health on the campuses of institutions of higher education. Such campaign shall be designed to—“(1) improve the general understanding of mental health and mental disorders;“(2) encourage help-seeking behaviors relating to the promotion of mental health, prevention of mental disorders, and treatment of such disorders;“(3) make the connection between mental and behavioral health and academic success; and“(4) assist the general public in identifying the early warning signs and reducing the stigma of mental illness.“(c) Composition.—The working group convened under subsection (b) shall include—“(1) mental health consumers, including students and family members;“(2) representatives of institutions of higher education;“(3) representatives of national mental and behavioral health associations and associations of institutions of higher education;“(4) representatives of health promotion and prevention organizations at institutions of higher education;“(5) representatives of mental health providers, including community mental health centers; and“(6) representatives of private-sector and public-sector groups with experience in the development of effective public health education campaigns.“(d) Plan.—The working group under subsection (b) shall develop a plan that—“(1) targets promotional and educational efforts to the age population of students at institutions of higher education and individuals who are employed in settings of institutions of higher education, including through the use of roundtables;“(2) develops and proposes the implementation of research-based public health messages and activities;“(3) provides support for local efforts to reduce stigma by using the National Health Information Center as a primary point of contact for information, publications, and service program referrals; and“(4) develops and proposes the implementation of a social marketing campaign that is targeted at the population of students attending institutions of higher education and individuals who are employed in settings of institutions of higher education.“(e) Definition.—In this section, the term ‘institution of higher education’ has the meaning given such term in section 101 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001).“(f) Authorization of Appropriations.—To carry out this section, there are authorized to be appropriated $1,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2018 through 2022.”
.

fable.w: The Secretary must convene a working group whose required members include non-federal parties (mental health consumers, students, family members, and representatives of colleges, associations, and providers), and that group plans a federal public education campaign. The tempting reading is that this is only intra-government coordination, because of the word "interagency" and the collaboration with the CDC Director. That reading fails because subsection (c) mandates outside members, so the group works like an advisory panel that brings outsiders into a federal decision.
fable.s: shall convene an interagency, public-private sector working group to plan, establish, and begin coordinating and evaluating a targeted public education campaign

qwen_block.w: The section requires the Secretary to convene a working group to plan a public education campaign. Subsection (c) explicitly mandates that this group include non-federal entities such as mental health consumers, students, family members, representatives of higher education institutions, and private-sector groups. This constitutes participation by outside parties in the federal decision-making process regarding the campaign's design and implementation.
qwen_block.s: (c) Composition.—The working group convened under subsection (b) shall include—“(1) mental health consumers, including students and family members;“(2) representatives of institutions of higher education;“(3) representatives of national mental and behavioral health associations and associations of institutions of higher education;“(4) representatives of health promotion and prevention organizations at institutions of higher education;“(5) representatives of mental health providers, including community mental health centers; and“(6) representatives of private-sector and public-sector groups with experience in the development of effective public health education campaigns.

opus.w: The Secretary must convene a working group that includes mental health consumers, students, family members, college representatives, associations and private-sector groups, all outside the federal government. The group plans and helps run a federal campaign and develops a plan for it, so outsiders shape a federal decision. Calling this mere outreach or intra-agency coordination is wrong: the group is 'interagency' but also explicitly 'public-private', and subsection (c) requires non-federal members.
opus.s: shall convene an interagency, public-private sector working group to plan, establish, and begin coordinating and evaluating a targeted public education campaign
opus.b: The tempting wrong reading is that this is a public education campaign rather than a policy decision, so the working group is just outreach. That reading fails. The Secretary must convene a "public-private sector working group" to plan and establish a federal campaign. The group must include people from outside the government, such as consumers, students, family members, colleges and advocacy groups. That is the kind of advisory body with non-federal members that the definition counts.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a working group that includes non-federal members such as mental health consumers, students, family members, and representatives from private-sector groups and institutions of higher education. This group is convened to plan and coordinate a public education campaign, which constitutes an advisory body with outside participation as defined by the inclusion of non-federal entities in the decision-making or planning process.
qwen_chat.s: (c) Composition.—The working group convened under subsection (b) shall include—“(1) mental health consumers, including students and family members;“(2) representatives of institutions of higher education;“(3) representatives of national mental and behavioral health associations and associations of institutions of higher education;“(4) representatives of health promotion and prevention organizations at institutions of higher education;“(5) representatives of mental health providers, including community mental health centers; and“(6) representatives of private-sector and public-sector groups with experience in the development of effective public health education campaigns.
qwen_chat.b:
Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the working group includes "mental health consumers" and "representatives of institutions of higher education," this constitutes participation. However, the definition states that participation involves consulting with people *outside* the government. While some members are outside, the group is convened by the Secretary to plan a campaign, which is an advisory role. But wait, the definition says: "Participation might happen in an advisory board, committee, or commission... It does not include applications for benefits or grants." The key is whether the outside parties are involved in a *federal decision*. Here, the working group plans a public education campaign. Is planning a campaign a "decision"? The definition says "consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." The working group's plan is likely advisory to the Secretary. The definition explicitly includes "advisory committee, board, or panel that includes non-federal members". This working group fits that description. It includes non-federal members (students, family members, private sector reps). Therefore, it is participation.

Wait, let's re-read the "No" traps. "consultation or coordination BETWEEN federal agencies... is not participation". This is not just between agencies. It includes private sector. "advisory committee... that includes non-federal members". This is an advisory working group with non-federal members. So it is "Yes".

Let's double check if "working group" is considered an advisory committee. The definition says "Participation might happen in an advisory board, committee, or commission, but it can be other things too." It also says "consult or coordinate with people outside of the government before making a decision." The working group plans the campaign. The Secretary then presumably implements it. This is coordination/consultation with outsiders.

Let's look at the "No" trap: "reports to, or notifications of, Congress...". Not applicable. "applications for benefits...". Not applicable.

Is there a reason to say "No"? Maybe if the working group is just internal? No, subsection (c) explicitly lists "mental health consumers", "representatives of institutions of higher education", "private-sector... groups". These are outside the federal government.

Therefore, the label is "Yes".
